description:
tests/client_tests.rs:889-903 builds a JmapResponse with a Mailbox/get invocation carrying a real RFC-shape payload (accountId, state, list, notFound), calls extract_response::<serde_json::Value>, then asserts only:

  assert!(val.is_ok(), 'extract_response must succeed: {val:?}');

A regression in extract_response that returned Ok(Value::Null) — for example, if the deserializer were short-circuited or the value path inverted — would pass this test. The fixture payload is right there at line 894; tightening to assert!(val.expect("...").as_object().unwrap().contains_key("accountId")) is one line and forecloses the false-pass class.

Same shape issue at tests/client_tests.rs:382-411 (test_call_round_trip): the test asserts session_state, method_responses.len(), method_responses[0].0 (method name), and method_responses[0].2 (call_id), but does NOT inspect method_responses[0].1 (the args payload). The fixture in tests/fixtures/jmap/call_response.json contains the args; a regression that stripped or zeroed the args would not be caught.

Both tests have the necessary fixture data already; tighten the assertions.
title: test_extract_response_success only asserts is_ok(); does not inspect returned Value
